questions.prompt: A colleague asks «Кто согласовал смету?» (kto sag-la-SO-val SMYE-too), 'who approved the estimate?'. Which reply answers that question the way Russian arranges it?
questions.correction: Both sentences are grammatical, but only the first answers the question. Russian puts new information at the end, and the new information here is the actor, so the actor stands last: Смету согласовал директор (SMYE-too sag-la-SO-val dee-RYEK-tar). The distracter is the neutral order, which answers «что сделал директор?», 'what did the director do?'. Learners keep English subject-first order and expect intonation to carry the answer; written Russian has no intonation to carry it, which is why lesson 101 treats position as grammar rather than style.

questions.prompt: A colleague promised to send the file and did not. Which sentence carries the reproach 'you did promise'?
questions.correction: же is an усилительная частица, an intensifying particle that points at something already known or already agreed between the speakers, and that shared background is what turns a report into a reproach: Ты же обещал (ty zhe a-bee-SHCHAL), 'you did promise'. Without же the sentence is a flat statement of fact and sounds like a note in a file. Note the spelling: же is written separately, never with a hyphen, which is the opposite of -то. The distracter is the sentence a learner produces when translating 'you promised' word for word and leaving the shared expectation unmarked.

questions.prompt: Say that nobody said anything at the meeting. Which sentence is grammatical Russian?
questions.correction: Russian requires multiple negation: if the verb is negated, the indefinite pronouns in the same clause must be negated too, so никто, ничего and не said all stand together: Никто ничего не сказал (neek-TO nee-che-VO ne ska-ZAL). The distracter copies English, where a single negative is enough and a second one cancels the first. Spanish speakers have an advantage here, because Spanish also allows and often requires concord, but the Russian set has to be complete: leaving не off the verb is the error, not adding it.

questions.prompt: Turn «Если я знаю, я звоню» (YEs-lee ya ZNA-yoo, ya zva-NYOO), 'if I know, I call', into a counterfactual about the past: 'if I had known, I would have called'.
questions.answer: Если бы я знал, я бы позвонил.
questions.distractor: Если бы я знаю, я бы звоню.
questions.correction: бы is invariable and combines with a past-tense form, not with a present-tense one, because the subjunctive has no tense or person marking of its own: the past form supplies the lexical event and бы supplies the unreality. So the correct sentence is Если бы я знал, я бы позвонил (YEs-lee by ya ZNAL, ya by paz-va-NEEL). The distracter keeps the present tense, which is the single commonest error with бы, and it usually comes from translating 'if I know' and then adding бы as if it were a separate word for 'would'.

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence so that it means 'He loves his own work': «Он любит ___ работу».
questions.correction: свой points back to the subject of the clause, so свою работу is work belonging to him: Он любит свою работу (on LYO-beet sva-YOO ra-BO-too). его would say that he loves someone else's work, and it is indeclinable, so it would not change even though работа is feminine accusative. The agreement is with the possessed noun, not with the possessor: свою is feminine accusative because работа is feminine accusative, whichever person owns it. Learners who have drilled его and её as 'his' and 'her' reach for them here and quietly change the meaning of the sentence.

units.title: Word formation: prefixes that change the verb, suffixes that predict a noun, adjectives and adverbs from one stem, evaluative forms, and decoding an unseen word

lessons.title: Verb prefixes that change the verb: за-, пере-, от-, раз-, до-, недо-
lessons.explanation: An underived Russian verb is imperfective, and prefixing it makes it perfective: that is the single most productive fact in Russian word formation, and alphaDictionary states it as a principle, 'Underived Russian verbs are basically imperfective' and 'Prefixing an underived verb makes it perfective'. The new perfective then needs an imperfective mate, which is usually built with the suffix -ыва- or -ива-, and the accent falls on the syllable before that suffix. So писать (pee-SAT), 'to write', imperfective, gives написать (na-pee-SAT), perfective, and the derived perfective переписать (pee-ree-pee-SAT), 'to rewrite', needs переписывать (pee-ree-PEE-sy-vat) for repeated rewriting. Notice what happens to the stress: it moves back one syllable, from the ending onto the stem, and it stays there in every form of the new imperfective. Notice too what happens to a stem vowel: if the syllable before the suffix contains о, it changes to а, so заработать (za-ra-BO-tat) gives зарабатывать (za-ra-BA-ty-vat), while рассказывать keeps its а because the vowel is already there. The prefixes themselves are a small inventory with stable meanings, and the meanings are mostly metaphorical extensions of space. за- marks the beginning of an action, as in заговорить (za-ga-va-REET), 'to start talking', or the enclosing of an object, as in запаковать (za-pa-ka-VAT), 'to pack up'. пере- marks excess, as in переработать (pee-ree-ra-BO-tat), 'to overwork' or 'to rework', and it also marks 'again' and 'outdo', as in переписать and переспорить (pee-ree-SPO-reet), 'to outargue'. от- marks separation and sending away, as in отправить (at-PRA-veet), 'to send off', and открыть (at-KRYT), 'to open'. раз- marks dispersal and undoing, as in разобрать (ra-za-BRAT), 'to take apart', and распаковать (ras-pa-ka-VAT), 'to unpack'. до- marks completion to the end, as in дописать (da-pee-SAT), 'to finish writing', and недо- marks insufficiency, as in недописать (ned-a-pee-SAT), 'to leave unfinished'. That last triple is the one to memorise as a set: дописать means you reached the end, недописать means you fell short, переписать means you did it again or too much. Spelling follows two rules that ru.wikipedia sets out. Prefixes in the first group are always written the same way, and недо- belongs to that group. Prefixes ending in з or с are written with з before voiced consonants and vowels and with с before voiceless consonants, which is why the same prefix appears as раз- in разобрать and рас- in распаковать.
lessons.example: A short account of a piece of work, with the prefixes doing the narrative. Сначала я записал черновик. Потом переписал его начисто. Выводы я не дописал: не хватило данных. Коллега распаковал архив и переслал мне таблицы. Два раздела мы недоделали. (sna-CHA-la ya za-pee-SAL cheer-na-VEEK. pa-TOM pee-ree-pee-SAL ee-VO NA-chee-sta. VY-va-dy ya ne da-pee-SAL: ne KHVA-tee-la DAN-nykh. ka-LYE-ga ras-pa-ka-VAL AR-kheef ee pee-ree-SLAL mnye TAB-lee-tsy. dva raz-DYE-la my ned-a-DYE-la-lee.) 'First I wrote a draft. Then I rewrote it fair. I did not finish the conclusions: there was not enough data. A colleague unpacked the archive and forwarded me the tables. We left two sections unfinished.' Now the same account as a process description, where the imperfectives are required because the actions are repeated: Каждый день я записываю черновик, переписываю его начисто и дописываю выводы. Коллега распаковывает архив и пересылает мне таблицы. (KAzh-dy dyen ya za-PEE-sy-va-yoo cheer-na-VEEK, pee-ree-PEE-sy-va-yoo ee-VO NA-chee-sta ee da-PEE-sy-va-yoo VY-va-dy. ka-LYE-ga ras-pa-KO-vy-va-yet AR-kheef ee pee-ree-SY-la-yet mnye TAB-lee-tsy.) 'Every day I write a draft, rewrite it fair and finish the conclusions. A colleague unpacks the archive and forwards me the tables.' Compare the two versions word by word. The perfective series записал, переписал, дописал reports single completed acts in sequence, which is why the account reads as a narrative. The imperfective series записываю, переписываю, дописываю reports a routine, which is why it reads as a procedure; lesson 85 made the same distinction between aspect in narrative and aspect in instruction. The negative sentence «не дописал» is the place where the prefix does semantic work rather than aspectual work: дописать means to reach the end, so negating it says the end was not reached, while «недописал» would say the writing stopped short of the required amount, which is a judgement about sufficiency rather than about completion. Both are possible in this paragraph, and the difference is whether the writer ran out of time or ran out of data. Finally, the prefixes in the second paragraph are the same inventory in the same order, which is the practical payoff: learn six prefixes and you can generate the vocabulary of a whole workflow.
lessons.question: A learner writes «Вчера я переписываю отчёт» and explains that пере- means 'again'. What is wrong, and what does the sentence need?
lessons.answer: переписывать is the secondary imperfective of переписать, so it cannot report a single completed act yesterday; the sentence needs the perfective «Вчера я переписал отчёт».
lessons.distractor: Nothing is wrong, because the prefix пере- already carries the perfective meaning and the suffix -ыва- is optional.
lessons.correction: The suffix is not optional and the prefix does not carry aspect on its own. Prefixation produced a perfective, переписать, and the -ыва- suffix produced a second imperfective from it, переписывать, which is used for repeated or ongoing rewriting. A single completed act yesterday takes the perfective, so «Вчера я переписал отчёт» is the sentence. The distracter inverts the mechanism: it treats the prefix as the aspect marker and the suffix as decoration, when the suffix is precisely what undoes the perfectivity that the prefix created. The stress is the audible signal: переписа́ть has it on the ending, перепи́сывать has it on the syllable before the suffix.

depth.definitions: An underived verb is one with no prefix, and in Russian such verbs are imperfective by default. Prefixation is the addition of a prefix, which perfectivises the verb and usually adds a meaning. Secondary imperfectivisation is the creation of a new imperfective from a prefixed perfective, normally with -ыва- or -ива-. An aspectual pair is a perfective and an imperfective that name the same event, and a prefix that adds no meaning beyond perfectivity (на-, по-, с- in many verbs) creates a 'pure aspectual' pair, while a prefix with a meaning creates a new verb that then needs its own pair. Prerequisites: the aspect system of lessons 56 to 59, the motion-verb prefixes of lesson 67, which are the spatial origin of the meanings used here, and the verbal nouns of lesson 84, since -ние nouns are built from the same stems.
depth.mechanism: The system is a two-stage machine. Stage one adds a prefix to an underived imperfective, and the result is perfective with a new meaning: писать 'write' becomes переписать 'rewrite'. Stage two adds -ыва- or -ива- to that perfective, and the result is imperfective again, with the same new meaning: переписывать 'rewrite repeatedly or habitually'. Every prefixed verb you meet in a text has been through stage one, and most have a stage-two partner, so the practical question is always which stage the text needs. The prefix meanings are not arbitrary: they are spatial relations applied to actions. за- is 'behind, enclosed, begun'; пере- is 'across, beyond, again'; от- is 'away from'; до- is 'as far as'; недо- is 'not as far as'; раз- is 'apart'. When you meet an unfamiliar prefixed verb, read the prefix as a spatial preposition and the base as an action, and the meaning usually falls out: распаковать is 'apart' plus 'pack', and that is unpacking. The accent rule follows from the suffix: -ыва- carries no stress of its own and pulls the stress onto the syllable before it, which is why the imperfective is regularly one syllable further back than the perfective.
depth.secondExample: A customer service exchange where four prefixes carry the whole history of an order. «Заказ отправили, но недоплатили за доставку.» (za-KAS at-PRA-vee-lee, no ned-a-pla-TEE-lee za da-STAF-koo.) 'The order was sent, but the delivery was underpaid.' «Мы пересчитали сумму и доплатили разницу.» (my pee-ree-schee-TA-lee SOOM-moo ee da-pla-TEE-lee RAZ-nee-tsoo.) 'We recalculated the amount and paid the difference.' «Посылку распаковали и переупаковали заново.» (pa-SYL-koo ras-pa-ka-VA-lee ee pee-ree-oo-pa-ka-VA-lee ZA-na-va.) 'The parcel was unpacked and packed again.' Three observations. First, the pair недо- and до- is a minimal contrast in meaning with the same base: недоплатить is to pay less than owed, доплатить is to pay the remainder, and пересчитать is to count again, so the three prefixes map onto three stages of one transaction. Second, all the verbs are perfective and the sequence is a narrative of completed steps, which is the register of a complaint or a resolution, not a procedure. Third, распаковали and переупаковали contain the spelling alternation раз- and рас- before voiced and voiceless consonants, and the same prefix appears in two shapes in one sentence. A learner who hears only the base платить will understand 'paid' three times and miss that one payment was short, one was a top-up and one was a recalculation.
depth.mistake: Five errors recur. The first is using a prefixed perfective for habitual action, as in «Каждый день я переписал отчёт», where the routine needs переписываю. The second is assuming that the prefix only perfectivises and therefore ignoring its meaning, which turns недоплатить into 'pay' and переписать into 'write'. The third is confusing до- with недо-: дописать is to finish, недописать is to fall short, and the difference is a judgement the text may depend on. The fourth is misplacing the stress in the secondary imperfective, saying переписа́вать instead of перепи́сывать, which is the error the accent rule predicts and the one that most marks a foreign accent in this vocabulary. The fifth is overgenerating: inventing a prefixed verb that Russian does not have, such as *записать in the sense of 'to finish writing', where the language uses дописать. English speakers make the second error most often because English phrasal verbs suggest that the particle is optional colour; Spanish speakers, whose prefixes are fewer and less productive, tend to avoid prefixed verbs altogether and then sound vague where Russian is precise. Diagnostic: for every prefixed verb, name the prefix meaning and the base meaning separately, then decide whether the sentence needs the perfective or the imperfective stage.
depth.application: Choose one verb you use every day, such as писать, читать or работать, and build a six-line table with the prefixes за-, пере-, от-, раз-, до- and недо-. For each line write the prefixed perfective, its secondary imperfective, the meaning, and one sentence about your own work. Then check the stress on every imperfective and mark the syllable before -ыва-. Finally, write a six-sentence account of a real task you completed last week, using at least four different prefixes, and then rewrite the same account as a weekly routine, converting every verb to its secondary imperfective. The pair of texts is the exercise: the first is a narrative, the second is a procedure, and the only thing that changes is the stage of the machine.
depth.summary: An underived Russian verb is imperfective, and a prefix makes it perfective and adds a meaning. The new perfective then takes -ыва- or -ива- to become imperfective again, with the stress on the syllable before the suffix and with о changing to а where the rule applies. The prefixes are a small spatial inventory: за- beginning or enclosing, пере- across or again or excess, от- away, раз- apart, до- as far as the end, недо- short of the end. The triple дописать, недописать, переписать is the fastest way to feel the difference between completion, insufficiency and repetition. Spelling follows the voicing rule for раз- and рас-, and недо- is always written the same. Learn the prefixes as meanings and the aspect as a two-stage machine, and unfamiliar verbs become readable.

visual.title: Prefix inventory table with aspect partners
visual.description: A labeled five-column table: prefix, core spatial meaning, example verb, secondary imperfective, and one sentence of use. Rows for за-, пере-, от-, раз-, до- and недо-. Rendered as text steps, not as an image.
steps: Step 1, draw the header row. Five columns: приставка, значение, perfective, imperfective, пример. Leave the last column for a sentence of your own, because the table only becomes yours when you have written in it.

Step 2, fill the spatial meanings first. Write 'beginning or enclosure' for за-, 'across, again, excess' for пере-, 'away' for от-, 'apart' for раз-, 'as far as the end' for до-, 'short of the end' for недо-. Do not write English translations of whole verbs yet; the point of the column is the spatial image.

Step 3, fill the pairs. For each prefix write one perfective and its secondary imperfective, for example переписать and переписывать, and put an accent mark on the imperfective. Check that the stress sits on the syllable before -ыва- in every row; any row that breaks the pattern is a row you have mis-analysed.

Step 4, add the minimal triple. Below the table write three lines, дописать, недописать, переписать, with the same base and three prefixes, and label them 'reached the end', 'fell short', 'did again or too much'. This is the row that fixes the semantic contrasts.

Step 5, add the spelling box. In a corner write раз- and рас- side by side with разобрать and распаковать, and note the voicing rule. Then write недо- alone and mark it 'always the same'. The table is complete when every row has a pair, a stress mark and a sentence.

lessons.title: Noun suffixes and what they predict: -ость, -ство, -ние, -тель, -ник
lessons.explanation: A Russian noun built with a suffix tells you three things before you look it up: what kind of thing it is, what gender it has, and therefore how it declines. That is the practical value of this lesson, and it is why the suffixes are worth learning as a system rather than one at a time. Start with the abstract quality nouns in -ость. They are built from adjectives, they are feminine, they end in a soft sign, and the stress normally stays where the adjective had it: возможный (vaz-MOZH-ny) gives возможность (vaz-MOZH-nast), 'possibility'; ответственный (at-VYET-stvee-ny) gives ответственность (at-VYET-stvee-nast), 'responsibility'; новый (NO-vy) gives новость (NO-vast), 'piece of news'. Because the ending is -ость and not -о, the noun declines as a feminine soft-stem noun: ответственности, ответственностью, об ответственности. The second family is -ство, which builds nouns of quality and collectivity and is neuter: качество (KA-chest-va), 'quality'; общество (OB-shchest-va), 'society'; производство (pra-ees-VOT-stva), 'production'; студенчество (stoo-DYEN-chest-va), 'the student body'. The third is -ние and its variant -тие, which build action nouns from verbs and are neuter: решение (ree-SHYE-nee-ye), 'decision', from решить; развитие (raz-VEE-tee-ye), 'development', from развить; чтение (CHTYE-nee-ye), 'reading', from читать; открытие (at-KRYE-tee-ye), 'discovery, opening', from открыть. The fourth is -тель, masculine, and it names the person or the device that does the action: читатель (chee-TA-tyel), 'reader'; преподаватель (preep-da-VA-tyel), 'teacher'; двигатель (DVEE-ga-tyel), 'engine'; выключатель (vy-klyoo-CHA-tyel), 'switch'. The fifth is -ник, also masculine, and it names a person by their work or an object by its function: работник (ra-BOT-neek), 'worker'; справочник (SPRA-vach-neek), 'reference book'; задачник (za-DACH-neek), 'problem book'; холодильник (kha-la-DEEL-neek), 'refrigerator'. A sixth, -ка, is feminine and builds either an action or the thing that results from it: подготовка (pad-ga-TOF-ka), 'preparation'; зарядка (za-RYAD-ka), 'exercise, charging'; закупка (za-KOOP-ka), 'purchase, procurement'. Two rules of thumb follow. Gender is predictable from the suffix, so -ость and -ка are feminine, -ство and -ние are neuter, -тель and -ник are masculine, and a reader who knows the suffix never has to guess an ending. And meaning is predictable from the base: an adjective plus -ость is an abstract quality, a verb plus -ние is the action or its result, a verb plus -тель is the doer or the instrument. The suffixes are productive, which means you can build a word and be understood even if the word is not in the dictionary, but productive does not mean unrestricted: each base has its conventional family, and the dictionary decides which member of the family exists.
lessons.example: A job advertisement, which is the genre where these suffixes cluster. Основные требования: ответственность, аккуратность и готовность к обучению. Обязанности: подготовка отчётов, работа с поставщиками, участие в разработке регламентов. Работодатель гарантирует обучение и развитие. (as-nav-NY-ye TRE-ba-va-nee-ya: at-VYET-stvee-nast, a-koo-RAT-nast ee ga-TOV-nast k ab-oo-CHEH-nee-yoo. a-bee-ZAN-nas-tee: pad-ga-TOF-ka at-CHO-taf, ra-BO-ta s pas-TAF-shchee-ka-mee, oo-CHA-stee-ye v raz-ra-BOT-kye reeg-la-MYEN-taf. ra-BO-ta-da-tyel ga-ran-TEE-roo-yet ab-oo-CHEH-nee-ye ee raz-VEE-tee-ye.) 'Main requirements: responsibility, accuracy and readiness to learn. Duties: preparation of reports, work with suppliers, participation in the development of regulations. The employer guarantees training and development.' Read the ad as a suffix inventory and it becomes transparent. ответственность, аккуратность and готовность are three -ость nouns built from adjectives, all feminine, all naming qualities the employer wants. обучение is a -ние noun from обучать, 'to teach', and it appears twice, once as the thing the candidate is ready for and once as the thing the employer guarantees. подготовка is a -ка noun from подготовить and names the action of preparing. разработка is another -ка noun, this time from разработать, and it names the process. работодатель is -тель on the base работода-, 'employer', and it is the mirror image of работник, the -ник noun for the employee. развитие is a -тие noun from развить. Five suffixes, one page, and every noun's gender is settled before the reader reaches the verb.
lessons.question: You meet the unfamiliar noun «согласованность» (sag-la-SO-van-nast) in a contract. What can you say about it without a dictionary, and what can you not say?
lessons.answer: The suffix -ость makes it a feminine abstract noun of quality, built from an adjective, declining as a soft-stem feminine, and it most likely means 'consistency, coherence'; what you cannot know is the precise legal sense the contract gives it, which only the context and the definition clause supply.
lessons.distractor: The suffix -ость makes it an adverb, so it modifies a verb and means 'consistently'; the sentence will tell you which verb it modifies.
lessons.correction: -ость never builds adverbs. Adverbs from adjectives are built with -о, as lesson 108 sets out, and they do not decline; a word ending in -ость is a noun and it declines through the whole feminine paradigm. The distracter confuses the two most productive endings in the language, and the confusion is expensive because the noun is the subject or object of a clause while the adverb is a modifier. What the suffix does tell you is real: feminine, abstract, quality, built from an adjective. What it does not tell you is the technical sense, which is why a contract reader still checks the definition.

depth.definitions: A suffix is a morpheme added after the root that changes the word's meaning or its word class. Russian distinguishes word-building suffixes, which create a new word (работ-ник from работа), from form-building suffixes, which create a form of the same word (the past-tense -л-, the comparative -ее-). The Russian Wikipedia article on suffixes states that division and lists the form-building set separately, which matters because a form-building suffix never changes the gender or the dictionary entry. An abstract noun names a quality or a state rather than a thing (возможность, качество). An action noun names the action or its result (решение, подготовка). An agent noun names the person or instrument that performs the action (читатель, выключатель). Prerequisites: gender and adjective agreement from lesson 41, the case system from lessons 51 to 54, the verbal nouns introduced in lesson 84, and the aspect pairs of lesson 106, because -ние nouns are usually built from the perfective stem.
depth.mechanism: The mechanism is class change plus gender assignment, and both are carried by the suffix. A suffix that derives a noun from an adjective has to give the noun a gender, and Russian assigns it by the shape of the ending: -ость ends in a soft sign and takes feminine agreement, -ство ends in -о and takes neuter, -ние ends in -е and takes neuter, -тель and -ник end in a consonant and take masculine, -ка ends in -а and takes feminine. This is why the suffixes are a reading tool and not just a vocabulary list: the ending is the gender, and the gender is the declension. The meaning side works by base plus category. An adjective names a property, so adjective plus -ость names the property as a thing. A verb names an action, so verb plus -ние names the action as a thing, and verb plus -тель names whoever performs it. The system is productive because the categories are open: any adjective of the right shape can produce an -ость noun, and any transitive verb can produce a -ние noun, which is why new technical vocabulary enters Russian through these suffixes rather than through borrowing. The limits are lexical rather than grammatical: the language has conventional families, and a newly built word may be understood and still be wrong for the register.
depth.secondExample: An abstract from a management report, where the -ние chain does the compressing. «Внедрение новой системы требует оценки рисков и согласования с исполнителем. Руководство ожидает сокращения сроков и повышения качества.» (vnee-dRYE-nee-ye NO-vay sees-TYE-my TRE-boo-yet a-TSEN-kee REE-skaf ee sag-la-sa-VA-nee-ya s ees-pal-NEE-tye-lem. roo-ka-VOT-stva a-zhee-DA-yet sa-kra-SHCHEH-nee-ya SRO-kaf ee pa-vy-SHEH-nee-ya KA-chest-va.) 'The introduction of the new system requires an assessment of risks and agreement with the contractor. Management expects a reduction in deadlines and an improvement in quality.' Every content noun here is a derived action noun: внедрение, оценка, согласование, сокращение, повышение, and руководство is a -ство collective. That is not decoration. Each -ние noun compresses a clause into a phrase, which is exactly the device lesson 84 described, and it is why written Russian can pack six propositions into two sentences without a single finite verb. Note the case government that comes with the compression: требует оценки (genitive), ожидает сокращения (genitive), согласования с исполнителем (genitive plus с plus instrumental). A learner who expands the abstract into speech has to undo all of it: «Мы внедряем систему, поэтому нужно оценить риски и согласовать условия с исполнителем. Руководство ожидает, что сроки сократятся, а качество повысится.» The vocabulary is the same family; the grammar is the spoken register.
depth.mistake: Four errors recur. The first is assigning the wrong gender, usually by translating the English word rather than reading the ending, so that ответственность is treated as neuter because 'responsibility' has no gender in English. The second is confusing -ость with -о, which turns an abstract noun into an adverb: «Он ответил с ответственностью» is correct, «Он ответил ответственностью» is not, and «Он ответил ответственно» is the adverb. The third is overgeneralising the derivational pattern and inventing forms the language does not use, for example *возможность as a countable plural in every context, or *читательство for 'readership' where Russian says читательская аудитория. The fourth is stress: -ние nouns frequently shift the stress from the verb stem to the suffix, реши́ть to реше́ние, разви́ть to разви́тие, while -тель nouns keep the stem stress, чита́ть to чита́тель. English speakers make the first two constantly because their language gives no gender cue; Spanish speakers make the first less often, since Spanish also assigns gender, but they transfer Spanish suffixes and produce *ответственidad-shaped errors in the other direction, using -ация for nouns that Russian builds with -ние. Diagnostic: read the ending, name the gender, name the category, and only then reach for the dictionary.
depth.application: Take a page of Russian you have already read in this course, ideally a report or an advertisement, and underline every noun of more than five letters. For each one write the suffix, the base word and the gender, and check the gender against the agreement in the sentence. You should find that the ending predicted the agreement every time; where it did not, you have found either a compound or an irregular noun, and both are worth a note. Then build a six-row table of your own professional vocabulary, one row per suffix, and fill it with words from your own field, checking each in a dictionary before you use it. Finally, write a five-sentence paragraph about your work in the written register, using at least four derived nouns and no more than two finite verbs, then rewrite it in speech with finite verbs and clauses. That pair of texts is the lesson's real test.
depth.summary: Russian noun suffixes encode category and gender at the same time. -ость builds feminine abstract qualities from adjectives and declines as a soft-stem feminine; -ство builds neuter qualities and collectives; -ние and -тие build neuter action nouns from verbs; -тель and -ник build masculine agents and instruments; -ка builds feminine actions and their objects. The base predicts the meaning and the ending predicts the declension, so an unfamiliar noun of this shape can be read before it is looked up. Stress moves towards the suffix in many -ние nouns and stays on the stem in -тель nouns. The written register lives on these nouns, which is why expanding them into clauses is the first move of any summary.

visual.title: Suffix to gender to declension: a three-column reading map
visual.description: A labeled text diagram with one row per suffix, showing the base it attaches to, the category it creates, the gender it assigns, and one model noun with its genitive. Rendered as text steps, not as an image.
steps: Step 1, set the columns. Five columns: суффикс, основа, категория, род, образец. The fourth column is the one that saves you in a text, because gender decides every ending that follows.

Step 2, fill the adjective row. Put -ость in column one, прилагательное in column two, 'abstract quality' in column three, 'feminine' in column four, and возможность with its genitive возможности in column five. Mark the soft sign as the gender signal.

Step 3, fill the verb rows. Put -ние with глагол, 'action or result', 'neuter', решение and решения. Then -тель with глагол, 'agent or instrument', 'masculine', читатель and читателя. Then -ка with глагол, 'action or object', 'feminine', подготовка and подготовки.

Step 4, add the collective row. Put -ство with существительное or прилагательное, 'quality or collectivity', 'neuter', общество and общества, and note that this suffix often attaches to nouns rather than verbs, which is why it is the odd one out in the table.

Step 5, add a stress column beside the model. Write the verb or adjective the noun came from and mark where the stress stood: реши́ть to реше́ние, чита́ть to чита́тель. The map is complete when every row explains both the gender and the stress of its model.

lessons.title: Adjectives and adverbs built from one stem: -н-, -ск-, -ов-, -лив- and the adverb in -о
lessons.explanation: Russian builds adjectives mostly by suffixation, and the Russian Wikipedia article on the adjective says so directly: adjectives are most often formed with suffixes, its example being болото to болотный. Four suffixes cover most of what a learner meets. -н- attaches to nouns and produces a plain relational adjective: вкус to вкусный (VKOOS-ny), 'tasty'; лес to лесной (lees-NOY), 'forest, of the forest'; болото to болотный (ba-LOT-ny), 'marsh, of the marsh'. -ск- attaches to nouns, very often to place names and to nouns denoting people or institutions, and produces an adjective of relation: город to городской (ga-rat-SKOY), 'urban, city'; Россия to российский (ra-SEE-skee), 'Russian, of Russia'; творчество to творческий (TVOR-ches-kee), 'creative'. -ов- and its variant -ев- attach to nouns and produce a possessive or material adjective: берёза to берёзовый (bee-RYO-za-vy), 'birch, made of birch'; бой to боевой (ba-ee-VOY), 'combat'. -лив- attaches to nouns and verbs and produces a quality adjective with the sense of 'given to': забота to заботливый (za-BOT-lee-vy), 'caring'; совесть to совестливый (SO-vees-lee-vy), 'conscientious'. The important division is not between suffixes but between adjective types. Качественные adjectives name a quality that can vary in degree, and only they have short forms, comparatives and adverbs in -о. Относительные adjectives name a relation to something and have none of those: городской has no short form, no comparative and no adverb in -о, and a learner who writes *городск or *городское in a short-form slot has applied the wrong paradigm. The adverb is built from the qualitative adjective with -о: быстрый to быстро (BYST-ra), уверенный to уверенно (oo-VYE-ren-na), краси́вый to краси́во (kra-SEE-va). A -ск- adjective does not take -о; it takes -ски, as the Russian Wikipedia article on the adverb shows with its own example, творческий to творчески, and when the adverb is formed with the prefix по- the result is hyphenated: по-русски (pa-ROOS-kee), 'in Russian', по-английски (pa-an-GLEE-skee), 'in English'. Two spelling rules complete the picture. After ш, ж, ч and щ the adverb ending is -о under stress and -е without it: горячо (ga-ree-CHO), 'hotly', свежо (svee-ZHO), 'freshly', but блестяще (blees-TYA-shche), 'brilliantly'. And the short form of an -н- adjective drops the final -н and inserts -ен in the masculine: вкусный to вкусен (VKOO-seen), уверенный to уверен (oo-VYE-reen), while the feminine, neuter and plural keep the full stem: вкусна, вкусно, вкусны.
lessons.example: A short report of a meeting, then the same content in a review, so that the adjectives and the adverbs can be compared. Городской совет подготовил подробный отчёт. Обсуждение было долгим, но спокойным. Мы быстро нашли компромисс и уверенно представили его комиссии. В зале стало тихо. (ga-rat-SKOY sa-VYET pad-ga-TO-veel pad-ROB-ny at-CHOT. ab-soozh-DYE-nee-ye BYE-la DOL-geem, no spa-KOY-nym. my BYST-ra nash-LEE kam-pra-MEES ee oo-VYE-ren-na preed-STA-vee-lee ee-VO ka-MEE-see-ee. v ZA-lye STA-la TEE-kha.) 'The city council prepared a detailed report. The discussion was long but calm. We quickly found a compromise and presented it to the commission confidently. The room went quiet.' Now the same events as a service review, where the adjective and adverb pairs are visible side by side: Обслуживание было внимательным, но оформление шло медленно. Сотрудник отвечал вежливо и подробно, однако система работала нестабильно. (ab-SLOO-zhee-va-nee-ye BYE-la vnee-MA-tyel-nym, no a-farm-LYE-nee-ye shlo MYED-len-na. sat-ROOD-neek at-vee-CHAL VYEZH-lee-va ee pad-ROB-na, ad-NA-ka sees-TYE-ma ra-BO-ta-la nee-sta-BEEL-na.) 'The service was attentive, but the paperwork went slowly. The employee answered politely and in detail, however the system worked unreliably.' Three mechanical facts are worth extracting. First, the adjectives городской and подробный are of different types: городской is relational and could not be used in the short form, while подробный is qualitative and appears in the review as подробно, the adverb. Second, the adverbs быстро, уверенно, медленно, вежливо and нестабильно all modify verbs and are built with -о from the neuter stem, and not one of them agrees with anything, which is the formal test that separates an adverb from a short adjective. Third, the short forms in «Обсуждение было долгим, но спокойным» are instrumental, because было requires the instrumental for a predicate adjective, and the endings -им and -ым are the masculine and neuter instrumental, not the adverb ending. A learner who writes «Обсуждение было долго» has produced an adverb where a short adjective belongs, and the sentence then says that the discussion existed slowly rather than that it was long.
lessons.question: A learner writes «Работа была практично, но творческо». What are the two errors, and how do you repair them?
lessons.answer: Both words should be adverbs or short adjectives of the right type: the natural repair is «Работа была практичной, но творческой», using the instrumental short form of the qualitative adjectives; if the meaning is about how the work was done, «Работа шла практично и творчески» uses the adverbs, with -ски for the -ск- adjective.
lessons.distractor: The sentence is correct, because -о is the adverb ending and adverbs can stand after было.
lessons.correction: было in this construction is a copula and takes a predicate adjective, not an adverb, so the slot requires the instrumental short form: практичной, творческой. The second error is the formation of the adverb from a -ск- adjective with -о: творческий gives творчески, never *творческо, and the Russian Wikipedia article on adverbs gives this exact pair as its model of suffixal formation. Note the difference in meaning between the two repairs: «Работа была практичной» evaluates the work, «Работа шла практично» describes the manner of doing it. The distracter treats -о as a universal adverb marker, which is the single most common formation error in this lesson.

depth.definitions: A качественное adjective names a quality that admits degrees: быстрый, вкусный, уверенный. An относительное adjective names a relation to a substance, a place, a time or an institution and does not admit degrees: городской, болотный, российский. A притяжательное adjective names an owner: мамин, отцов. Only qualitative adjectives have short forms (быстр, вкусен, уверен), comparatives (быстрее) and adverbs in -о (быстро). An adverb is an invariable word that modifies a verb, an adjective or another adverb, and the Russian Wikipedia article on adverbs classifies its formation as suffixal (быстрый to быстро, творческий to творчески), prefixal and prefixal-suffixal. A short adjective is the predicate form of a qualitative adjective, and after было, будет and in the present tense with a zero copula it stands in the instrumental or the nominative depending on the construction. Prerequisites: adjective agreement from lesson 41, comparison from lesson 43, the impersonal predicatives of lesson 62, and the suffix inventory of lesson 107, which this lesson continues on the adjective side.
depth.mechanism: The mechanism is a division of labour between the two word classes, and the endings enforce it. An adjective agrees with a noun, so it carries gender, number and case; an adverb agrees with nothing, so it has one form. That is why the test for an adverb is negative: if the word changes when you change the noun, it is an adjective. The suffixes decide which adjectives can feed which constructions. A relational adjective names a relation, and a relation cannot be more or less intense, so городской has no comparative and no short form; the grammar follows the semantics. A qualitative adjective names a degree-able quality, so it feeds the short form, the comparative and the adverb, and the adverb is built from the neuter short form stem with -о, which is why быстро looks like the neuter short form быстро but behaves differently: the short form agrees with a neuter noun, the adverb agrees with nothing. The -ск- adjectives sit on the relational side, and their adverbs take -ски because -ск- is part of the stem rather than a gender ending. The hyphen in по-русски follows from the same history: по- is a prefix added to a -ски adverb, and prefixed -ски adverbs are written with a hyphen, as the spelling section of the adverb article states.
depth.secondExample: A performance review, where the same person is described once with adjectives and once with adverbs, and the register changes with the choice. «Сотрудник внимательный и ответственный. Его отчёты подробные и точные.» (sat-ROOD-neek vnee-MA-tyel-ny ee at-VYET-stvee-nay. ee-VO at-CHO-ty pad-ROB-ny-ye ee TOCH-ny-ye.) 'The employee is attentive and responsible. His reports are detailed and accurate.' «Сотрудник работает внимательно и ответственно. Он пишет подробно и точно.» (sat-ROOD-neek ra-BO-ta-yet vnee-MA-tyel-na ee at-VYET-stvee-nay. on PEE-shet pad-ROB-na ee TOCH-na.) 'The employee works attentively and responsibly. He writes in detail and accurately.' Four observations. First, the adjective version evaluates the person and the product, which is the register of a formal appraisal; the adverb version evaluates the work, which is the register of a reference or a conversation. Second, the endings are doing the same job in both: -ый and -ий agree with сотрудник and отчёты, while -о and -но agree with nothing. Third, ответственный gives ответственно and внимательный gives внимательно, both with the stress in the same place as the adjective, which is the normal pattern for -тельн- adjectives. Fourth, the choice between the two versions is not stylistic decoration: a review that says «он внимательный» makes a claim about character, and a review that says «он работает внимательно» makes a claim about conduct that is easier to evidence, which is the same discipline lesson 95 applied to hedging.
depth.mistake: Five errors recur. The first is using an adverb where a predicate adjective belongs, as in «Работа была практично», which comes from the absence of a copula distinction in English. The second is forming an adverb from a -ск- adjective with -о, producing *творческо and *практическо instead of творчески and практически. The third is giving a relational adjective a short form or a comparative, as in *городск or *городскее, which the semantics forbid. The fourth is forgetting the inserted -ен in the masculine short form, writing *вкусный in a predicate slot instead of вкусен, or *уверенн instead of уверен. The fifth is the hyphen in по-русски and по-английски, which learners omit because the prefix feels separate. Spanish speakers have an advantage with the adjective and adverb distinction, since Spanish también separates rápido from rápidamente, but they transfer the Spanish adverb in -mente and produce forms like *быстромеntе only in the first weeks; the more durable transfer is stress, because Spanish adverbs keep the adjective stress and Russian adverbs from mobile-stress adjectives do not, as in дорого́й to до́рого. Diagnostic: change the noun's gender and see whether the word changes; if it does, it is an adjective, and then check whether the adjective type allows the form you have built.
depth.application: Take eight nouns from your own field and build an adjective from each with the suffix that fits, checking the result in a dictionary before you trust it. Then sort your eight adjectives into qualitative and relational, and for the qualitative ones write the short masculine form, the comparative and the adverb. You should end with three short columns and a clear sense of which adjectives refuse the forms. Next, write a six-sentence review of a service you actually used, using four adverbs and two short adjectives, and mark every word that agrees with a noun. Finally, rewrite the review as a formal appraisal using adjectives instead of adverbs, and compare the two versions for what they claim about the person as opposed to the work. That comparison is the point of the lesson.
depth.summary: Adjectives are built by suffix: -н- and -ск- for relation, -ов- for material and possession, -лив- for disposition. Only qualitative adjectives have short forms, comparatives and adverbs in -о, and relational adjectives such as городской have none of the three. Adverbs are invariable and are built from qualitative adjectives with -о, from -ск- adjectives with -ски, and with a hyphen when the prefix по- is added. After sibilants the adverb ending is -о under stress and -е otherwise, and the masculine short form inserts -ен. The test that never fails is agreement: if the word changes with the noun, it is an adjective.

visual.title: One stem, two word classes: the agreement test
visual.description: A labeled text diagram with three columns: the adjective with its noun, the same word after a verb, and the verdict. A second block shows the -ск- branch and the hyphen branch. Rendered as text steps, not as an image.
steps: Step 1, write the adjective row. Put быстрый ответ, быстрая машина, быстрое решение and быстрые шаги in one column, and mark the ending that changes in each line. These four lines establish that the word is agreeing with a noun.

lessons.title: Evaluative suffixes: diminutive and augmentative, and when size is not about size
lessons.explanation: Russian nouns carry an evaluation inside the word, and the suffixes that add it are among the most frequent in speech. The Russian Wikipedia article on the diminutive defines the category as a word or word form conveying a subjective evaluation of small volume or size, usually by means of diminutive affixes, and then makes the point this lesson is built on: the meaning of smallness can be accompanied by various emotional and expressive colourings, of affection (уменьшительно-ласкательная форма, as in кошечка) or of disparagement (уменьшительно-пренебрежительная форма, as in людишки, народишко). The inventory is small enough to learn as a set. -ик and -чик make a masculine diminutive: дом to домик (DO-meek), шкаф to шкафчик (SHKAF-cheek), ключ to ключик (KLYOO-cheek). -ок and -ёк do the same with a stressed ending: друг to дружок (droo-ZHOK), угол to уголёк (oo-ga-LYOK). -очка and -ечка make a feminine diminutive, often with a shift of meaning: чашка to чашечка (CHA-shech-ka), книга to книжечка (KNEE-zhech-ka), минута to минуточка (mee-NOO-tach-ka). -еньк- and -оньк- attach to adjectives and to names: маленький (MA-leen-kee), тихонько (tee-KHON-ka), Машенька (MA-shen-ka). On the augmentative side, -ище makes a big or imposing thing: дом to домище (da-MEE-shche), дождь to дождище (dazh-DEE-shche). The disparaging set includes -ишк- and -онк-: дом to домишко (da-MEESH-ka), книга to книжонка (knee-ZHON-ka). Gender is the part learners get wrong, and the rule is that the suffix usually inherits the base's gender rather than overriding it. домик is masculine because дом is masculine; чашечка is feminine because чашка is feminine; домище is masculine because дом is masculine, so the careful written form is «огромный домище» (ag-ROM-ny da-MEE-shche), not «огромное домище», even though the word ends in -е. The same trap appears in -ишко, which ends in -о but is masculine when the base is masculine: домишко declines as домишка, домишку, and takes masculine agreement, «старый домишко» (STA-ry da-MEESH-ka). A noun ending in -о is normally neuter, and this is the exception worth memorising, because the ending looks like a neuter and the dictionary says otherwise; neuter agreement with these words does occur in speech, but it is not the written norm. The pragmatics matter more than the size. A diminutive in a service exchange is politeness rather than measurement: «Можно ещё чашечку?» (MOZH-na yesh-CHO CHA-shech-koo), 'could I have another cup?', asks for a small cup and signals a small request. Минуточку (mee-NOO-tach-koo) means 'just a moment' and is not a claim about sixty seconds. A diminutive can also be ironic: «Хорошенькое дело!» (kha-RO-shen-ka-ye DYE-la), 'a fine business!', means the opposite of fine. And it can soften a criticism, which is why a negative judgement delivered with a diminutive sounds less like an attack and more like a shared joke.
lessons.example: A short description of a flat, then a service exchange, because the two registers use the same suffixes differently. Вот наш домик. Рядом стоит огромный домище соседа. В углу шкафчик, на столе чашечка и ложечка. (vot nash DO-meek. RYA-dam sta-EET ag-ROM-ny da-MEE-shche sa-SYE-da. v oog-LOO SHKAF-cheek, na sta-LYE CHA-shech-ka ee LO-zhech-ka.) 'Here is our little house. Next to it stands the neighbour's enormous house. In the corner there is a little cupboard, on the table a little cup and a little spoon.' Now the counter: «Можно ещё чашечку кофе?» (MOZH-na yesh-CHO CHA-shech-koo KO-fye?) 'Could I have another cup of coffee?' «Минуточку, сейчас принесу.» (mee-NOO-tach-koo, see-CHAS pree-nee-SOO.) 'Just a moment, I will bring it now.' «А водички можно?» (a va-DEECH-kee MOZH-na?) 'And could I have some water?' «Конечно, конечно.» (ka-NYESH-na, ka-NYESH-na.) 'Of course, of course.' Read the first text as a lesson in gender. домик is masculine because дом is masculine, and «наш домик» shows it. домище is also masculine, which is why the adjective is огромный and not огромное: the ending -е is the neuter nominative ending in most nouns, but this noun belongs to the masculine second declension, and the dictionary gender wins over the look of the ending. шкафчик keeps the masculine of шкаф, and чашечка and ложечка keep the feminine of чашка and ложка. Read the second text as a lesson in pragmatics. чашечку is not a request for a smaller vessel; it is the polite form of the request, and the same is true of водички, where the partitive genitive in -и and the diminutive work together. минуточку is a fixed politeness formula. A learner who replaces all three with the neutral forms, «Можно ещё чашку кофе?», «Минуту», «А воду можно?», will be understood and will sound slightly abrupt, which is exactly the register point that lesson 97 made about requests.
lessons.question: A learner writes «У них огромное домище» because the word ends in -е. What has gone wrong, and what is the form to write?
lessons.answer: The ending has been read as neuter, but домище is a masculine noun of the second declension inherited from дом, so the careful written form is «У них огромный домище».
lessons.distractor: Nothing has gone wrong, because every noun in -е is neuter and takes a neuter adjective.
lessons.correction: -е is the usual neuter nominative ending, but it is not a reliable gender signal in derived nouns. The augmentative -ище builds a masculine noun from a masculine base, and домище declines as домища, домищу, домищем, which is the masculine pattern, not the neuter one. The agreement follows the noun's gender, so огромный is the form a careful writer uses. Neuter agreement with домище can be heard in speech, and some speakers extend the neuter pattern by analogy with words like училище, but the dictionaries give masculine and the written norm follows them. The distracter is the rule of thumb a learner builds after a month of Russian, and this lesson exists because the rule of thumb fails precisely where the suffix is most expressive.

depth.definitions: An evaluative suffix adds the speaker's attitude to a noun rather than naming a new object. Diminutives (уменьшительные) present the referent as small, and they divide into уменьшительно-ласкательные, affectionate, and уменьшительно-пренебрежительные, disparaging. Augmentatives (увеличительные) present the referent as large or excessive. The productive diminutive suffixes are -ик, -чик, -ок, -ёк, -ец, -очка, -ечка, -еньк-, -оньк-; the augmentative is -ище, with -ин- as a colloquial variant; the disparaging set includes -ишк- and -онк-. Evaluative suffixes are a subtype of word-building suffix, and they differ from the suffixes in lesson 107 in that they do not change the lexical category of the base: a diminutive of a noun is still a noun. Prerequisites: noun gender and agreement from lesson 41, the second declension from lessons 51 to 54, and the request register of lesson 97, which this lesson extends into a lexical resource.
depth.mechanism: The mechanism is evaluation by morphology rather than by a separate word. English needs an adjective, 'little', 'dear little', 'great big', or a change of tone, and the adjective can be removed; Russian builds the evaluation into the noun, so it cannot be removed without changing the word. That is why diminutives are so frequent in speech and so rare in formal writing: they are a single-word way of doing what English does with a phrase, and phrases are what formal prose prefers. Gender works by inheritance, and the inheritance is lexical rather than phonological: the derived noun keeps the declension class of its base, which is why домище belongs to the masculine second declension despite ending in -е, and why домишко belongs to the same class despite ending in -о. The ending is a spelling fact; the declension is a grammatical one, and only the dictionary or the agreement in a model sentence tells you which applies. The pragmatic mechanism is distance. A diminutive reduces the imposition of a request, which is why it appears in service encounters; applied to a person or an institution it can reduce respect, which is why the same suffix can be affectionate or contemptuous depending on the target and the tone.
depth.secondExample: A conversation where the same base produces affection in one line, pity in the next and irony in the third, which is the test of whether you have understood the category. «Смотри, какой симпатичный домишко.» (smat-REE, ka-KOY seem-pa-TEECH-ny da-MEESH-ka.) 'Look, what a nice little house.' «Домишко-то старый, крыша течёт.» (da-MEESH-ka-ta STA-ry, KRY-sha tee-CHOT.) 'The little house is old, and the roof leaks.' «А у соседа домище, но ипотека на тридцать лет.» (a oo sa-SYE-da da-MEE-shche, no ee-pa-TYE-ka na TREE-tsat let.) 'And the neighbour has a huge house, but a mortgage for thirty years.' «Хорошенькое дело: домище есть, а ремонта нет.» (kha-RO-shen-ka-ye DYE-la: da-MEE-shche yest, a ree-MON-ta nyet.) 'A fine business: the big house is there, but there is no renovation.' Four points. First, домишко is masculine in every line, which is why the adjective is симпатичный and старый and not симпатичное and старое. That is the same trap as домище, in the opposite spelling: an -о ending on a masculine noun. Second, the difference between the first two lines is carried by the adjective and the tone, not by the suffix, which is why the article says the colouring varies: the suffix supplies the smallness and the speaker supplies the attitude. Third, домище is masculine and would take огромный if an adjective were present, and the sentence avoids the issue by using есть, which is worth noticing as a writer's habit: when the gender of an expressive noun is uncertain, use a construction that does not require agreement. Fourth, хорошенькое дело is a fixed ironic formula, and its diminutive has nothing to do with size: it means the opposite of good.
depth.mistake: Four errors recur. The first is treating every evaluative suffix as a diminutive, which turns домище into a small house and голосище into a small voice. The second is reading the ending as the gender, producing «огромное домище» and «старое домишко» where the dictionaries give masculine agreement. The third is mis-stressing -ок and -ёк, saying ДРУ-жок instead of дру-ЖОК, and mis-stressing -ище, saying ДО-мище instead of до-МИ-ще. The fourth is register: overusing diminutives in formal writing, where «отчётчик» or «договорчик» reads as either childish or sarcastic. English speakers make the first error because English diminutives are lexical and rare, so they look for a size meaning and stop there; Spanish speakers make it differently, since Spanish has productive diminutives in -ito and -illo, and they transfer the affectionate reading into contexts where Russian intends contempt, producing a warm tone in a sentence meant to be dismissive. Diagnostic: ask what the speaker is doing with the word, not what size the object is, and check the noun's dictionary gender before you write an agreeing adjective.
depth.application: Take six everyday nouns around you and write the diminutive and the augmentative of each, then check each derived noun's gender in a dictionary and write one agreeing adjective beside it. You should find that the gender follows the base almost every time and that the ending can mislead you, which is the habit this exercise builds. Next, write three short exchanges: one service request using two diminutives, one affectionate description of a place, and one ironic comment using хорошенькое дело or a -ишк- noun. Read them aloud and decide which you would say to a stranger, which to a friend, and which to nobody. Finally, take a formal paragraph you wrote earlier in this course and check that it contains no evaluative suffixes; if it does, decide whether the register allows them, and remove the ones that do not.
depth.summary: Evaluative suffixes build the speaker's attitude into the noun. Diminutives (-ик, -чик, -ок, -очка, -ечка, -еньк-) present smallness, affection or, with -ишк- and -онк-, contempt; the augmentative -ище presents size or excess. Gender is inherited from the base, so домик, домище and домишко are all masculine even though the last two end in -е and -о; check the dictionary before writing an agreeing adjective. In speech the suffixes do pragmatic work: they soften requests, signal affection or carry irony, and the same suffix can do all three. In formal writing they are rare, because the written register prefers explicit adjectives. Learn the set as evaluations rather than sizes, and let the dictionary gender decide the agreement.

lessons.title: Capstone: decoding an unseen word in a real text
lessons.explanation: This lesson puts the level together as a procedure. You will meet words you have never seen, and the procedure lets you read them before you look them up: strip the ending, identify the prefix, identify the suffix, find the root and a cognate you know, decide where the head of a compound is, and only then confirm the meaning in context and in a dictionary. The order matters, because each step constrains the next. Stripping the ending gives you the stem and, for a noun, the gender: -ость is feminine, -ние is neuter, -тель and -ник are masculine, and a final -а on a derived noun is feminine. The prefix inventory is the one from lesson 106, and the meanings are spatial: за- beginning or enclosure, пере- across or again, от- away, раз- apart, до- to the end, недо- short of the end, вы- out, при- towards, у- away. The suffix inventory is the one from lessons 107 to 109, and it gives the category: -ость an abstract quality, -ние an action, -тель an agent or instrument, -ник an agent or object, -ск- a relation, -ищ- size. The root is what remains, and the root is where your existing vocabulary pays: if you know писать, you can read записывать, переписывать and недописанный without a dictionary. Compounds add one more rule, and it is the rule learners most often invert: in a Russian compound the last stem is the head and the first stem modifies it, so самолётостроение is a kind of строение, building, namely aircraft building, and not a kind of aircraft. The linking vowel is -о- after hard stems and -е- after soft ones, which is why самолёт plus строение gives самолётостроение and нефть plus переработка gives нефтепереработка. Abbreviations need the same discipline with a different inventory. The Russian Wikipedia article on abbreviations divides them into сложносокращённые слова, built from the shortened beginnings of the words of a phrase, and инициальные аббревиатуры, built from initial letters or sounds, and the initial type divides again into letter-named, sound-named and mixed. МГУ is letter-named, эм-гэ-у (em-ghe-OO), and it expands to Московский государственный университет. вуз is sound-named, and it is read as an ordinary word, vuz, because the sounds permit it, which is why it is written in lower case and declines: в вузе. Минэкономразвития is сложносокращённое, built from министерство экономического развития, and its head is министерство, which is why the word is neuter and takes neuter agreement. That last point is the practical test: agreement tells you which part of a compound or abbreviation is the grammatical head, and the head tells you what kind of thing the word names.
lessons.example: Here is a real sentence from a TASS report of 23 October 2025, followed by its decoding. «Минэкономразвития в сентябре понизило прогноз роста ВВП России на 2025 год до 1% с апрельских 2,5%.» (meen-ee-ka-na-mraz-VEE-tee-ya v seen-TYAB-RYE pa-NEE-zee-la prag-NOS RO-sta ve-ve-PE ra-SEE-ee na dve TY-sya-chee DVA-tsat PYAT gOt da ad-na-VO pra-TSEN-ta s ap-RYEL-skeekh dva TSEE-lykh pyat pra-TSEN-taf.) 'The Ministry of Economic Development in September lowered its forecast for Russia's GDP growth for 2025 to 1 percent from the April figure of 2.5 percent.' Now the procedure applied word by word. Минэкономразвития is a compound abbreviation: Мин- from министерство, эконом- from экономического, развития the full final word, and the head is министерство, which is why the verb понизило is neuter. понизило is по- plus низ- plus -и- plus -ло: the base is низкий, low, the prefix по- marks a small downward movement, and the -ло ending is the neuter past, agreeing with the neuter subject. прогноз is a borrowing you either know or look up, and it is the object of понизило. роста is the genitive of рост, growth, governed by прогноз: a forecast of growth. ВВП is an initial abbreviation, валовой внутренний продукт, gross domestic product, and it is indeclinable here because it stands in apposition to роста, which carries the ending. России is the genitive of Россия, governed by ВВП. на 2025 год is the prepositional phrase for the target year, and до 1% с апрельских 2,5% is the range of the revision, with до marking the new value and с marking the old one. Five steps, one sentence, and no dictionary was needed until прогноз, which is the only truly opaque item.
lessons.question: You meet «нефтепереработка» (nyef-tee-pee-ree-RAB-ka) in an article about industry. What is it, and which part of the word tells you?
lessons.answer: It is oil refining, the processing of oil: нефть is oil, переработка is processing, the head is переработка, and the linking vowel -е- marks the compound.
lessons.distractor: It is oil produced by processing, because the first stem names the product and the second stem describes how it was made.
lessons.correction: The head of a Russian compound is the last stem, and the first stem modifies it. переработка is processing, from переработать, to process or rework, and нефть narrows it to the processing of oil, so the word names an industry, not a product. The distracter reverses the dependency because English compounds often have the modifier first and the head last too, but the temptation here is to read the first noun as the subject of the second, which produces 'oil that has been processed' instead of 'the processing of oil'. The agreement test settles it: нефтепереработка is feminine and singular, agreeing with переработка, and a sentence about the industry will use verbs like выросла or сократилась, not the plural agreement you would need for a quantity of oil.

depth.definitions: Decoding is the process of deriving a word's meaning and grammatical properties from its morphology before consulting a dictionary. The stem is what remains after the inflectional ending is removed. A derivational prefix adds meaning to a stem and, for verbs, perfectivises it. A derivational suffix changes the category or adds an evaluation. A compound (сложное слово) combines two or more stems with a linking vowel. A сложносокращённое слово is an abbreviation built from the shortened beginnings of the words of a phrase, and an инициальная аббревиатура is built from initial letters or sounds; the letter-named type is read as letter names, the sound-named type as a word. The head of a compound or abbreviation is the element that determines the grammatical gender and the category. Prerequisites: the prefixes of lesson 106, the noun suffixes of lesson 107, the adjective and adverb suffixes of lesson 108, the evaluative suffixes of lesson 109, and the reading disciplines of lessons 81 to 85, which supply the register and inference skills that stop a plausible decoding from becoming a confident wrong answer.
depth.mechanism: The procedure works because Russian is agglutinative at the edges and fusional at the centre. The edges, prefixes and suffixes, are units with stable meanings that can be listed and recognised; the centre, the root, is where the idiosyncrasy lives. That is why decoding proceeds from the outside in: the ending gives gender and case, the suffix gives category, the prefix gives direction, and only then does the root have to be identified. Each step narrows the hypothesis space, and the narrowing is what makes an unfamiliar word tractable rather than intimidating. The head rule for compounds is a consequence of Russian's right-headedness: the second stem is the category and the first is the modifier, which is why a compound's gender is the gender of its last stem and why agreement in the sentence confirms the analysis. Abbreviations work the same way at a different level: the grammatical head is the word that was not abbreviated, or the first element if all were, and the agreement in the sentence is the only reliable signal. This is why the capstone insists on confirming a decoding against the sentence: a decoded word is a hypothesis, and agreement, case government and register are the evidence that tests it.
depth.secondExample: A second text, this time with two compounds that look symmetrical and are not. «Грузоперевозки выросли на восемь процентов, а нефтепереработка сократилась.» (groo-za-pee-ree-VOS-kee VY-ras-lee na VO-seem pra-TSEN-taf, a nyef-tee-pee-ree-RAB-ka sa-kra-TEE-las.) 'Freight haulage rose by eight percent, while oil refining declined.' Three points. First, грузоперевозки is plural because перевозки is plural, and the agreement выросли confirms it; нефтепереработка is singular feminine, and сократилась confirms that. The agreement is doing the same job as the dictionary, which is why a careful reader checks it before trusting a guess. Second, the two compounds have the same shape, noun plus linking vowel plus action noun, and opposite heads in terms of what they count: перевозки counts journeys or shipments and is plural, переработка names a process and is singular. A decoder who applied one pattern to both would produce 'freight processing' and 'oil haulage'. Third, both words belong to the written register of industry statistics, which is why they are compounds rather than phrases: the spoken version would say «перевозки грузов» and «переработка нефти», with the genitive doing the work that the compound does by composition. That alternation between compound and genitive phrase is the register switch of this whole level.
depth.mistake: Four errors dominate. The first is stopping at the root: a learner recognises нефть and stops, producing 'oil something' and then guessing from context, which is how confident misreadings begin. The second is reversing the head of a compound, reading самолётостроение as a kind of aircraft rather than a kind of building. The third is treating every abbreviation as letter-named and spelling it out, which fails on вуз and on the mixed types, and it also fails to notice that a сложносокращённое word declines while a letter abbreviation often does not. The fourth is ignoring agreement, which is the one signal that can confirm or refute a decoding without a dictionary: if the verb is neuter and your decoded head is masculine, the decoding is wrong. English speakers make the second error because English compounds are also right-headed but the habit of reading left to right as a phrase is strong; Spanish speakers make the third, since Spanish abbreviations are usually letter-named and read as such. Diagnostic: after decoding, say the word's gender, its category and its head aloud, then check each against the sentence before you write a translation.
depth.application: Take the TASS sentence in this lesson and produce a full gloss: for every word, the ending, the gender or case, the prefix and suffix if any, and a translation. Then do the same with one paragraph of a Russian text in your own field, at least five sentences, using a dictionary only after you have written your hypothesis for each unfamiliar word. Mark each hypothesis as confirmed or corrected, and count how many you got right before the dictionary. Finally, record a two-minute spoken explanation in Russian of one unfamiliar word you decoded, following the model in the example: name the parts, name the head, name the gender, and give one sentence of use. The written gloss and the spoken explanation are the two deliverables of the capstone, and the pair is the point: the same analysis, once for the eye and once for the ear.
depth.summary: An unfamiliar Russian word can be read before it is looked up. Strip the ending for gender and case, read the suffix for the category, read the prefix for the direction, and identify the root against vocabulary you already have. In a compound the last stem is the head and the first modifies it, with -о- or -е- as the linking vowel; in an abbreviation the head is the unabbreviated word or the first element, and the type decides whether it is read as letters or as a word. Agreement in the sentence is the test that confirms or refutes the analysis, which is why decoding is a hypothesis and not a translation. The level ends here with a procedure rather than a list: the lists are in lessons 106 to 109, and the procedure is what makes them usable on text you have never seen.

visual.title: Five-pass decoding worksheet for one sentence
visual.description: A labeled text diagram with five horizontal passes over the same sentence, each pass adding one layer of analysis: ending, suffix, prefix, root and head, then confirmation from agreement. Rendered as text steps, not as an image.
steps: Step 1, pass one, endings. Copy the sentence and circle every final ending. Write the case and number above each circle, and the gender beside every noun. This pass produces the grammatical skeleton and nothing else.

Step 2, pass two, suffixes. Underline every derivational suffix and write its category: -ость quality, -ние action, -тель agent, -ск- relation, -ищ- size. This pass tells you what kind of word each noun is, which is often enough to translate it loosely.

Step 3, pass three, prefixes. Box every prefix and write its spatial meaning: за- beginning, пере- across or again, от- away, до- to the end, недо- short of the end. This pass turns a vague verb into a directed one.

Step 4, pass four, roots and heads. Write the root under each stem and, for compounds and abbreviations, mark the head. Put a star beside every root you recognise from your own vocabulary; the starred roots are the ones that need no dictionary.

Step 5, pass five, confirmation. For every hypothesis, find the word in the sentence that agrees with it or governs it, and mark the hypothesis confirmed or corrected. The worksheet is finished when every word has a pass-five mark, because a decoded word without a confirmation is only a guess.
