questions.prompt: Which verb means 'to rewrite a text'?
questions.correction: пере- adds the meaning 'again, over' to the base писать (pee-SAT), 'to write', so переписать (pee-ree-pee-SAT) is 'to rewrite'. написать is merely the perfective of 'write' and says nothing about doing it again. Both are perfective, and each needs a secondary imperfective for repeated action, which is переписывать (pee-ree-PEE-sy-vat) and not *переписывать with the stress anywhere else: the stress moves to the syllable before -ыва-. The distracter is the form a learner picks when the prefix looks like a mere perfectiviser, which is exactly what на- is for this verb.

questions.prompt: Which word is the noun meaning 'possibility'?
questions.correction: -ость builds a feminine abstract noun from an adjective, so возможный (vaz-MOZH-ny), 'possible', gives возможность (vaz-MOZH-nast), 'possibility', and the stress stays where it was in the adjective. возможно is the adverb and the impersonal predicative, 'possibly, it is possible', and it cannot stand as the subject of a sentence. The distracter is the commonest confusion in this family because English 'possible' and 'possibly' are one word apart, while Russian separates them by a whole declension: the noun declines, the adverb does not.

questions.prompt: Complete «Он ___ ответил» so that it means 'He answered quickly'.
questions.correction: The adverb is built from the adjective stem with -о: быстрый (BYST-ry) gives быстро (BYST-ra), and it modifies the verb ответил. The distracter leaves the adjective in the masculine nominative, which would have to agree with a masculine noun and cannot modify a verb. Note that the stress stays on the stem in both forms, which is the normal pattern for adverbs in -о from adjectives with fixed stress; adjectives with mobile stress move it, as in дорого́й to до́рого (da-RO-goy to DO-ra-ga).

questions.prompt: Which word describes a big, imposing house rather than a small one?
questions.correction: -ище is augmentative: домище (da-MEE-shche) is a big, imposing house, and the suffix can carry admiration or disapproval as well as size. -ик is diminutive: домик (DO-meek) is a little house, and it is the form used affectionately or apologetically. Both attach to the same stem дом, so the choice is evaluative and not lexical. Learners who have met only -ик read every evaluative suffix as 'small' and then find домище in a text about a mansion and cannot place it; lesson 109 exists to stop that, and it also notes that the augmentative takes neuter agreement, not masculine.

questions.prompt: In a report you meet «недописал» (ned-a-pee-SAL). What does the prefix tell you about the writing?
questions.answer: It was done insufficiently, less than the norm required, and left incomplete.
questions.distractor: It was written again from the beginning.
questions.correction: недо- combines не- and до-, and it marks insufficiency: the action fell short of the required measure. недописать (ned-a-pee-SAT) is 'to leave unfinished, to write less than needed', and it is perfective. Writing again would be переписать, which has a different prefix and a different meaning. The distracter guesses from the general look of a prefix rather than from the inventory, and that guess is what lesson 106 trains you out of: недо- is a recognisable unit with one meaning, not an accident of spelling.

questions.prompt: Which of these sentences denies the object rather than the action?
questions.answer: Мария купила не билет, а абонемент.
questions.correction: не negates the constituent that follows it, and the following constituent here is билет, so the sentence denies the ticket and asserts the pass: Мария купила не билет, а абонемент (ma-REE-ya koo-PEE-la ne bee-LYET, a a-ba-nee-MENT). The distracter negates the verb phrase and says that no purchase happened at all, which is a different claim. Both sentences are correct Russian, so the question is not about grammaticality but about scope, which is the point of lesson 103 and the reason lesson 101 treats не as a positional word.

questions.prompt: Choose the particle: «___ ты знаешь, что он уехал?» meaning 'You do know that he left, don't you?'
questions.correction: ведь marks shared knowledge and a mild expectation of agreement, so Ведь ты знаешь (vyet ty ZNA-yesh) means 'you do know, after all'. ли is the interrogative particle and always stands second in its clause, turning a statement into a question of fact: Знаешь ли ты (ZNA-yesh lee ty), 'do you know?'. The distracter is chosen by learners who treat all short words as interchangeable question markers, but ли asks and ведь asserts.

questions.prompt: Which sentence says 'I have no time' in idiomatic Russian?
questions.correction: Possession and its absence are built with у plus the genitive and нет, not with иметь: У меня нет времени (oo mee-NYA nyet VRYE-mee-nee). иметь exists, but it is a bookish verb for having in the abstract and it does not take this construction; using it is the calque that every European language invites. The form времени is the genitive of время, one of the ten nouns in -мя that decline differently from ordinary neuters, and lesson 107 returns to that set when it treats nouns built with suffixes.

questions.prompt: Make «Я хочу уточнить один вопрос» polite in a written request.
questions.answer: Я хотел бы уточнить один вопрос.
questions.distractor: Я хочу бы уточнить один вопрос.
questions.correction: The polite conditional puts бы after a past-tense form of the verb, so Я хотел бы уточнить (ya kha-TEL by oo-tach-NEET), literally 'I would have liked to clarify'. This is the standard softened request in correspondence and it answers a question from lesson 97 about the written politeness register. The distracter attaches бы to a present-tense verb, which Russian does not do: бы combines with the past form, whose -л ending is what carries the person and number in this construction.

questions.prompt: You want to say that she showed a photograph of herself, and you want the sentence to be unambiguous. Which word do you use?
questions.correction: свою фотографию can only mean the photograph belonging to the subject, so Она показала свою фотографию (a-NA pa-ka-ZA-la sva-YOO fa-ta-GRA-fee-yoo) is unambiguous. её фотографию is genuinely ambiguous between 'her photograph' in the sense of ownership and 'a photograph of her', because её is indeclinable and carries no reference back to the subject. The distracter is not wrong grammar; it is the wrong tool when the point of the sentence is to fix the reference, and that distinction is what lesson 105 teaches.

questions.prompt: Which form is the secondary imperfective of переписать, used for repeated rewriting?
questions.correction: Prefixation perfectivises an underived verb, and the new perfective then needs an imperfective mate, which is built with -ыва- or -ива-: переписать (pee-ree-pee-SAT) gives переписывать (pee-ree-PEE-sy-vat), with the stress on the syllable before the suffix. The distracter is the perfective itself, and using it for repeated action is the aspect error lesson 56 warned about, now visible in the shape of the word rather than in a list of pairs.

questions.prompt: Complete «Он взял на себя ___ за проект» with the noun 'responsibility'.
questions.correction: The noun is ответственность (at-VYET-stvee-nast), built with -ость from ответственный, and it is feminine, which is why it stands in the accusative singular here after взял на себя. The distracter is the adjective, which would have to agree with a noun that is not there. The suffix predicts the gender: -ость nouns are feminine, -ство and -ние nouns are neuter, -тель and -ник nouns are masculine, so the ending of a derived noun tells you its declension before you look it up.

questions.prompt: Which sentence means 'He answered quickly and confidently'?
questions.correction: Adverbs modify the verb and are built with -о from the adjective stem: быстрый gives быстро, уверенный gives уверенно (oo-VYE-ren-na). The distracter leaves both words as adjectives in the nominative, where they would have to agree with a noun, and there is no noun for them to agree with. Note the spelling rule that appears in the second adverb: after a soft stem the ending is -енно, and after a sibilant under stress it is -о, as in горячо (ga-ree-CHO).

questions.prompt: In a café the idiomatic polite offer is «Хотите ___ кофе?» rather than the neutral measure. Which form fits?
questions.correction: чашечку (CHA-shech-koo) is the diminutive accusative of чашка, and in service encounters the diminutive is the polite, slightly warm form of an offer, not a statement about size. чашку is grammatical but flat, and in this slot it reads as a measure rather than as an invitation. The distracter is what a learner produces by taking the dictionary form and declining it correctly, which shows that correctness and register are separate achievements; lesson 109 treats the evaluative suffixes as a register resource for exactly this reason.

questions.prompt: You meet the word «самолётостроение» (sa-ma-LYO-ta-stra-YE-nee-ye) in an article. What is it?
questions.answer: Aircraft manufacturing, the industry of building aircraft.
questions.distractor: Air travel, the practice of flying as a passenger.
questions.correction: Decode it in three moves: самолёт (sa-ma-LYOT), 'aircraft', plus -о- as a linking vowel, plus строение from строить (STRO-eet), 'to build', with -ние marking an abstract noun. The head is the second element, so the word names a branch of production, not a practice. The distracter stops at the first element and guesses from it, which is the failure mode lesson 110 is written against: in a compound the last stem carries the category and the first stem narrows it.

questions.prompt: In «Минэкономразвития» (meen-ee-ka-na-mraz-VEE-tee-ya), which word is the grammatical head that tells you what the body is?
questions.correction: Минэкономразвития is a сложносокращённое слово, a compound abbreviation built from the beginnings of министерство экономического развития, and the head is министерство. That is why the word behaves as a neuter noun and why it can be the subject of a sentence about decisions. The distracter is the most semantically vivid part, and choosing it is the usual error with abbreviations: the vivid stem is not the grammatical head. Note that the abbreviation is declined in careful usage but often left invariable in journalistic text.

questions.prompt: A colleague writes «Отчёт переписан, выводы недописаны». What does the sentence tell you?
questions.answer: The report has been rewritten and the conclusions are incompletely written.
questions.distractor: Someone is rewriting the report and will finish the conclusions later.
questions.correction: Two forms do the work. переписан is a short passive participle, which reports a result with the agent suppressed, and недописаны adds недо-, the prefix of insufficiency, in the same short passive form. The sentence is therefore a result statement: the rewriting is finished and the conclusions fall short. The distracter reads the same words as a plan in progress, which ignores both the passive result meaning and the prefix; lesson 106 and lesson 83 are the two halves of that reading.
